blocks.text: EXPOSE and LABEL are metadata; USER changes who runs later instructions and the container; HEALTHCHECK defines a periodic in-container probe whose status Docker reports but does not act on.
Documents the listening port; `-P` uses it. It publishes nothing and doesn't restrict container-to-container traffic.

blocks.code:
RUN groupadd --system --gid 10001 app && useradd --system --uid 10001 --gid app --no-create-home app
USER 10001:10001

items: Numeric UID so Kubernetes runAsNonRoot can verify it.
COPY'd files stay root-owned (read-only code is good).
Writable dirs (cache, uploads) must exist and be chowned before USER; fresh named volumes inherit that ownership.

blocks.text: Use OCI keys (`org.opencontainers.image.source`, `.revision`, `.version`) for tooling and prune filters.

blocks.code:
HEALTHCHECK --interval=15s --timeout=3s --start-period=60s --retries=3 \
  CMD ["python","-c","import urllib.request,sys; sys.exit(0 if urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/healthz',timeout=2).status==200 else 1)"]

items: Exit 0 healthy, 1 unhealthy; start-period failures don't count.
slim/distroless have no curl: use the runtime you ship.
Keep it cheap: no LLM calls or vector searches.

blocks.text: Q: "Does EXPOSE publish a port, and does an unhealthy HEALTHCHECK restart the container?" A: "No to both. EXPOSE is documentation; -p publishes. Docker only reports health; restarts come from exits, or from orchestrators like Kubernetes liveness probes. Compose uses health for depends_on conditions."

items: Numeric non-root USER; chown writable dirs first.
Healthchecks must be cheap and local.
